en: The Sūtra on the Majestic Power of the Youth Kumbhīra, spoken by the Buddha.
Translated by the Great and Vast Wisdom Amoghavajra.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Buddha was staying in the Tuṣita Heaven, within the Pāriyātraka tree in the Nandana Grove.
The precious palace beneath the Citta tree;
the Tathāgata is the life-force of immeasurable wisdom,
regarding all sentient beings as his only child.
At that time, there were hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of great bodhisattvas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges,
as well as śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and those who had attained the fruits of the four paths.
Furthermore, there were hundreds of thousands of lights,
as well as immeasurable bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas,
and upāsikās; gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and others.
All who encountered this light experienced their body hairs standing on end;
the radiance of their own bodies was eclipsed and became invisible,
as was that of this trichiliocosm.
Reaching upward to the Heaven of the Thirty-three and downward to the eighteen layers of hells,
including all the suns, moons, Southern Dous, and Northern Beis.
Furthermore, the palaces of the devas, the palaces of the nāgas, and the abodes of the various ṛṣis and immortals—
all the palaces of the celestial Māras and the heretics—
trembled violently, and they all lost their own radiance.
His body trembled so violently that he could not support himself.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī rose from his seat and approached the place where the Buddha was.
Prostrating with his five limbs touching the ground at the Buddha’s feet,
he addressed the Buddha,
saying: "Today, the Tathāgata, by means of the power of great, correct, and universal knowledge, possesses sovereign majesty and virtue."
He universally radiated such light that the worlds of the ten directions all became golden in color.
Furthermore, there was the perimeter of the Pārijātaka tree.
To the abodes of the Buddhas of the past, numbering as many as the sands of ten million billion nayutas of Ganges Rivers;
to the abodes of the Buddhas of the present;
and to the palaces of the devas and the palaces of the nāgas.
The stars, the moon, the sun, and the heavenly demon Pāpīyān were all struck with great terror and fell prostrate upon the ground before the Greatly Awakened World-Honored One.
We pray that you will explain to us, the fourfold assembly, this power of sovereign mastery over divine light.
From the time of immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of Ganges-sands of past Buddhas,
as well as all present Buddhas— [we have witnessed it].
"We have never before beheld such a sign of divine light;
we pray that you will explain it for us.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, wishing to resolve his own doubts, [spoke thus].
Observing that the fourfold assembly was entirely filled with doubt and perplexity,
he wished to restate this meaning and spoke these verses:
The Great Hero, the Fierce World-Honored One, Lion-Furrowing King,
whose divine light pervades the ten directions— within the palaces of the devas and the nāgas,
among the stars, the moon, the sun, and the heavens, as well as within this trichiliocosm.
All have become golden in color; the majesty of both their own bodies and those of others has naturally vanished.
The fourfold assembly—gods, humans, asuras, and others—is struck with great terror. We pray only that you, O God among Gods, [will appear].
"Reveal this Dharma for my sake. At that time, after Mañjuśrī, the Prince of the Dharma, had spoken these verses,
there were again hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of devas, humans, asuras, and others within the assembled multitude.
The bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, humans, non-humans, and others were all filled with doubt;
they each rose from their seats and, with one voice and in unison, approached the place where the Buddha was.
And he spoke in verse:
"Excellent, O God among Gods! Having attained perfect enlightenment long ago, you have today gained mastery and universally radiate great light."
These lights are all five colors, obscuring the three thousandfold world system.
Since I have come from the distant past, I have never encountered such an auspicious omen.
I only pray that you, in your great compassion, will clearly explain this wondrous meaning.
When the devas and humans had spoken these verses,
they addressed the Buddha once more, saying: "World-Honored One,
we pray only that the World-Honored One will dispel our confusion and ignorance."
"O Greatly Compassionate One, please explain this to me quickly.
At that time, the light of the Tathāgata’s sun-like radiance returned and circled the Buddha three times,
then entered through the crown of his head and addressed the great assembly.
Today, the Tathāgata regards all sentient beings with compassion as he does Rāhula;
furthermore, he causes all beings to attain liberation from the sufferings and hardships of the three miserable realms.
When these words were spoken, [the earth shook].
In the assembly were six masters of non-Buddhist paths,
with the Nirgranthas as their leaders;
they rose from their seats and addressed the Buddha, saying:
Gautama previously stated that you would cause all sentient beings to be free from the sufferings of the three miserable realms;
yet you also said, "I have compassion for all sentient beings as I do for Rāhula."
All these matters are entirely false words.
You, Gautama, recently departed from the palace of the Śākyas and practiced the path for six years among the Snowy Mountains.
"Now you claim to have attained equal and perfect enlightenment and to turn the Great Wheel of Dharma;
you deceive all sentient beings, causing them all to fall into hell.
You, Gautama, though you belong to the Śākya clan,"
Having lived for a long time in the mountains, he studied many magical arts or the ways of demons and spirits.
He deceived sentient beings with falsehoods, craftily claiming, "I have attained the fruits of the Path.
Gautama, if you have indeed attained the fruits of the Path and possess all-encompassing wisdom, [then prove it].
"If you have attained the fruit of the Way and realized perfect enlightenment,
why is it that the Way comes and goes, and its arising and ceasing are not fixed?
Gautama, you are therefore not omniscient."
If you say that one who possesses all-knowledge is a "Sarvajña," then since Gautama already possesses immeasurable supernormal powers,
there are infinite sentient beings present in this assembly.
"How can those destined for hell be rescued?
At that moment, the six heretical teachers leaped into the air,
raising a great, fierce fire and unleashing a torrent of wind and rain.
At times he magically produces mountains of swords from his hands,
and at other times he produces fierce fires,
causing all those who come to hear the Dharma [to experience these].
All undergo great suffering and affliction;
sometimes they cause the trichiliocosm to tremble,
and at other times they cause the earth to split open, from which boiling brine gushes forth.
At times, he causes the pārijātaka trees in the Nandana Grove of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven to be completely shattered;
at other times, he conjures mountains in mid-air,
or lifts up great boulders.
At times, he would soar through the air toward the east, west, south, or north;
he moved, stood, sat, and lay down with complete mastery and without obstruction.
At that time, those in the assembly each spoke these words:
"In truth, the Tathāgata lacks omniscience compared to the non-Buddhists;
those non-Buddhists truly possess omniscience and are superior to the Tathāgata.
Furthermore, each of the assemblies of sentient beings spoke these words.
The śramaṇa Gautama recently departed from the palace of the Śākyas and went to the Snowy Mountains;
it is now said that he has attained Buddhahood.
Having attained Buddhahood, he must possess all-encompassing wisdom (sarvajñatā).
"That Gautama merely speaks of the emptiness of persons and the emptiness of phenomena—
this is impossible; we cannot accept his words in faith."
Since you have already attained perfect enlightenment,
why is it that Devadatta— your own paternal cousin—
is daily and nightly harassing you; why do you not subdue him?
If even that one person could not transform others,
how could he possibly transform humans, devas, and all bodhisattvas?
This non-Buddhist has been so for immeasurable kalpas.
Having cultivated and gathered inconceivable dharma-gates,
you now manifest such great sovereign power.
We shall quickly take refuge in the non-Buddhist paths.
"He is worthy to serve as our Great Upādhyāya.
Let us go quickly to him and receive instruction.
At that time, the Tathāgata sat cross-legged.
He entered the Samādhi of the Revolving Dhāraṇī.
From the tuft of hair between his eyebrows, he emitted a thousand rays of light;
within each ray of light were hundreds of thousands of transformation Buddhas.
He again emitted a thousand rays of light,
which illuminated this trichiliocosm,
reaching upward as far as the Heaven of Neither Perception nor Non-Perception.
It shone downward upon worlds as numerous as the sands of forty-two billion Ganges Rivers.
That light further illuminated Buddha-lands to the east as numerous as the sands of forty-two billion Ganges Rivers;
it universally illumined the east, west, south, north, the four intermediate directions, and the zenith and nadir.
At that time, the great earth in the ten directions shook in six ways,
and the heavens rained down a profusion of precious flowers.
From within this light, emanated Buddhas each produced various sounds.
Furthermore, they scattered priceless incense, each saying these words:
"Today, the Tathāgata, out of great kindness and great compassion,
manifests this auspicious sign out of pity for all sentient beings."
There are two kinds of such trembling:
first, great trembling;
second, slight trembling.
This refers to this trichiliocosm,
as well as Mount Sumeru, the Iron Ring Mountains (Cakravāḍa), Mount Mucilinda, and Mount Mahāmucilinda.
That which is shaken throughout is called a "minor trembling.
A "great trembling" refers to the great earth of the ten directions,
extending upward as far as worlds as numerous as the sands of forty-two billion Ganges Rivers.
Extending downward as far as the presence of the Tathāgata King of Pure and Stainless Radiance,
there were all the rivers, great oceans, small mountains,
great mountains, the solar palace, the lunar palace, the stars and constellations, and the various devas.
All were shaken, trembling in six ways; this great trembling is called a "great trembling.
At that time, the Buddhas of the ten directions, along with the great bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and others, all came together from every quarter like a gathering of clouds.
Each of these bodhisattvas was accompanied by twenty thousand attendants who came to the place where the Buddha was.
From the faces of all these bodhisattvas and the assembly of Buddhas,
rays of five-colored light were emitted.
It also shone universally throughout the worlds of the ten directions.
At that time, those various non-Buddhists became dazed, confused, and bewildered;
all their majestic splendor was eclipsed and completely vanished.
The cauldron of boiling water on that ground surged upward and transformed into the great Anavatapta Lake;
those sentient beings who were suffering there [were likewise transformed].
Each mounted upon a white jewel lotus and leaped forth from the earth;
these various non-Buddhists were transformed into masses of fire,
which consumed their own bodies as they ascended into the sky and departed.
At that time, the Buddhas of the ten directions and all the bodhisattvas each uttered this praise:
"Excellent, excellent, Great Hero, Valiant World-Honored One!
You are able to act as a great field of merit for all sentient beings."
He caused all the non-Buddhist practitioners to retreat and disperse,
and brought all sentient beings suffering in pain to liberation from that suffering.
Truly, one must marvel at the rarity of the World-Honored One, the Perfectly Awakened One!
At that time, when the assembled multitude saw this event,
they all looked upon him with virtuous eyes, each abandoning their heterodox minds;
they took refuge in the Buddha and sought all manner of wholesome things.
Through sincere repentance, each attained the realization of the fruits [of the path].
At that time, the Tathāgata addressed Mañjuśrī, saying:
"Good son, for immeasurable kalpas I have cultivated samāpatti."
To ensure that all sentient beings attain complete liberation,
the Tathāgata further possesses immeasurable and profound dhāraṇī gates,
which sever all karmic obstructions for all living beings.
"Good son, listen attentively now; I shall explain this for you.

As these words were spoken, the great assembly in this gathering, as well as the Buddhas of the ten directions, the great Bodhisattvas, the Śrāvakas, the Pratyekabuddhas, and the seers possessing the five supernatural powers, [all listened].
Before the Tathāgata, he made a great and vast vow,
saying to the Buddha: "World-Honored One,
today the Tathāgata, by the power of his great compassion..."
To manifest the perfection of the merit of great supernormal powers,
we, the assembly of attendants, also possess a great dhāraṇī that benefits sentient beings within the world of the five turbidities.
We only pray that the World-Honored One will permit us to speak these divine mantras offered by those bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas,
each manifesting their transformed appearances and the causal conditions of their original karmic deeds.
Possessing the sovereign power of supernatural penetrations for the benefit of sentient beings,
each and every bodhisattva spoke these words:
"This divine mantra of mine is capable of serving as a great field of merit for all living beings."
Before the Tathāgata, they presented their final offerings;
there were as many as eighty nayutas of beings, equal in number to the sands of the Ganges,
each of whom spoke thus:
At that time, the Tathāgata secretly transformed his own body within the great assembly into the form of the youth Kumbhīra,
one thousand feet tall and possessing a thousand heads.
His body produced a thousand arms, and he let out a great, roaring cry. Thereupon,
the various bodhisattvas who had come from the ten directions to offer incantations,
as well as the śrāvakas, vanished into the void and were no longer visible.
There was only the boy alone, with no one else present.
At that time, the Tathāgata addressed the great assembly:
"Do not be afraid; each of you should return to your respective places."
This Bodhisattva and all those who recite the incantations shall have their mental terrors entirely dispelled and shall manifest their true forms.
At that time, Ānanda rose from his seat.
He approached the Buddha and addressed him, saying,
"O Tathāgata, what power does that youth possess, and what wisdom has he cultivated,
such that he manifests such signs of supernatural power?"
The bodhisattvas and all sentient beings who had come from the ten directions, as well as the Tathāgatas,
each manifested their respective mantras and then all vanished;
there was only this single person alone, without fault.
At that time, Ānanda, wishing to restate this meaning,
spoke these verses:
"O World-Honored One, Great Sovereign, Your majestic virtue is without peer."
"From kalpas long ago, I have never heard such a thing.
I only pray that the Great Holy Honored One will clearly explain the reason why you have spoken these verses.
Having spoken this verse, he addressed the Buddha again.
"We pray that you will explain for us the characteristics of these supernormal powers.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Ānanda and the great assembly:
"Good sons, throughout immeasurable kalpas, I have practiced difficult austerities."
Possessing various kinds of knowledge and various kinds of wisdom for the sake of seeking the Dharma;
joyfully giving away one's head, eyes, marrow, and brain for the sake of seeking the True Dharma;
and having today attained perfect enlightenment and subdued the Māra of the desire realm.
Furthermore, I cause sentient beings of the five turbidities to hear this mantra of mine,
so that they may be led to distance themselves from the three miserable realms.
Good son, if there are any sentient beings— whether bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, male lay devotees, or female lay devotees— [who hear it...]
Desiring to accomplish the Great Dharma, they intend to transcend the world;
or, remaining within the world, they resolve to rescue others from great suffering and hardship;
or, within the world, they act as great kings of physicians.
One who wishes to skillfully heal all manner of illnesses,
or desires to subdue the devas and māras and restrain the non-Buddhists,
should for the period of two weeks keep a pure room empty.
On the full moon day of the waxing phase, smear the ground with fragrant mud and construct a mandala according to one's inclination;
place various kinds of fruits within it and offer gathered white flowers.
If it is winter and there are no flowers, [one should proceed otherwise].
Cut flowers from five-colored variegated silks and scatter them upon the altar.
Practice the Way and perform prostrations three times during the day and night.
Recite the mantra three thousand times daily and six thousand times at night.
When practicing the Way, one wears white robes and bathes once every three days.
When entering or leaving [the monastery], one wears separate garments of yellow silk and wraps the head.
The four corners of the altar were fashioned with cypress wood pillars;
on one side hung thirty-two banners of Hachiman (eight by four).
In the center of the altar were placed one hundred ceramic incense burners.
Burn aloeswood incense, frankincense, pine resin, and so forth.
During the night at the altar, one must carefully refrain from lighting lamps;
silently recite the mantra.
The practitioner should face west and begin reciting the mantra while standing, not sitting.
This should continue for seven full days, or up to fourteen days,
remaining free from all attachments and staying far away from women.
When staying overnight, one must occupy a single room alone;
do not lie down and sleep with others.
Furthermore, O son of good family, regarding the practitioner’s food and drink:
Do not allow women to perform this;
it must be performed by men and given to travelers.
When preparing food and firewood, they must also be perfumed with incense.
Regarding the selection of an auspicious time:
one should also take pure spring water for use.
As for the person preparing the food:
One should always recite the mantra.
As soon as the meal is prepared, one should place it in the vessel and seal it;
otherwise, malevolent spirits will devour its fragrant and delicious essence.
The practitioner finds no flavor in food.
Son of good family, if one relies upon and practices this,
they will awaken to and penetrate all things, reaching the profound and numinous beyond the superficial.
At that time, the Tathāgata, with the majestic power of his compassionate light, clearly proclaimed the secret words of the most supreme Dharma wheel, chanting slowly:
"Namo to the Buddha Mahāśvarabala-vaikurvaṇakāya-kumbhīra-kumāra-garjita-rāja."
Homage to the Buddha Śākyamuni, Great Sovereign of Pure Ocean-Banner Merit.
Homage to the Truly Perfectly Awakened One, the Stainless Buddha of the Forty-Eight Vows.
Homage to all Buddhas of the ten directions, whose transformation, response, and reward bodies are boundless;
whose names are Mingyouxian (Darkness-Illuminating) and Vajrapāṇi.
Listen well to this wondrous and sublime mantra for subduing the Māra kings and ascending to the bodhi of true enlightenment through this *Mūlakarma*.
I pray that the Bodhisattvas of the ten directions, the eighteen Dream Kings,
will each clearly listen as I proclaim this wondrous divine spell, the *dhāraṇī* for the ritual of subduing the celestial Māras by the Great Victorious Kumbhīra Youth.
Oṃ kṛtita ṭa ṭa ra vaḥ khe me hūṃ hūṃ. Upon the completion of this mantra, the three-thousandfold great thousandfold world system shook six times.
The Buddhas of the ten directions and all the Bodhisattvas have all realized the ultimate;

as well as the Bodhisattvas, Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, the six-fold transcendent sages (*ṣaḍabhijña*), the great beings of the three knowledges (*traividya*), the Pratyekabuddhas, and all the lesser Bodhisattvas.
All attained the path of perfect and true enlightenment.
From the sky, jeweled flowers rained down in profusion,
and fragrant winds blew throughout the entire Buddha-world.
Celestial drums resounded spontaneously;
waterfowl and jewel groves were found everywhere,
each emitting various kinds of wondrous sounds.
They praised the inconceivable spiritual powers of the Buddhas.
At that time, there was a bodhisattva in the assembly named Bhaiṣajyarāja,
who rose from his seat, joined his palms, and paid respectful homage.
He addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Tathāgata, you have spoken this sovereign, divine, and wondrous dhāraṇī;
all the Buddhas of the ten directions have crossed over by means of it."
Since long ago, I have never heard this mantra.
Throughout immeasurable kalpas,
I have also cultivated various great dhāraṇīs and the gates of samāpatti.
In the presence of immeasurable Buddhas,
I have long heard the teachings on the various dharani-doors;
I myself have also practiced and maintained them with mastery.
"We have never before heard that the Tathāgata possesses such a dhāraṇī.
World-Honored One, today we resolve our minds to practice and study this Dharma-gate."
"And to assist the Tathāgata in proclaiming and transforming sentient beings.
I only pray that the World-Honored One will grant me permission to receive and uphold [this teaching].
At that time, the World-Honored One praised him, saying:
Excellent, excellent, son of good family!
That you are able to resolve to practice within the secret treasury of the Tathāgata and to assist my Dharma—
now is precisely the right time.
"I shall quickly expound the Tathāgata’s knowledge and vision,
so that all sentient beings may surely attain liberation.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja and the fourfold assembly—
Hearing that the Buddha had granted his permission, they were all greatly rejoiced and listened with single-minded attention, receiving and upholding [the teaching].
Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, if there are sentient beings..."
Those who wish to remain in the world while further seeking the supramundane,
or who resolve their minds to protect and uphold the Tathāgata’s semblance-dharma during its period of extinction so that it shall not be severed,
may give rise to a great and fierce resolve.
Those who seek the Tathāgata’s meditative concentration and wisdom,
or those who wish to rescue sentient beings from suffering and hardship,
must first recite the Tathāgata’s divine mantra one hundred thousand times before practicing any other methods.
World-Honored One, if there is a practitioner who seeks to see one of worldly eloquence, wisdom, and talent,
they should take seven *harītakī* fruits and one large *liang* of white sandalwood, burn them until they are reduced to ash.
Each bead should be individually burned with white honey;
for each bead, further make seven pellets,
totaling forty-nine pellets (seven times seven).
Recite the mantra over the medicine one thousand and eight times before an image of Śākyamuni.
Take one pill at dawn, continuing until the medicine is exhausted over a period of seven weeks.
All that exists within the body consists of thirty-six repositories:
hair of the head, hair of the body, nails, teeth, skin,
flesh, blood, sinews, veins, marrow, bones, heart, lungs, spleen, and kidneys.
The liver, gallbladder, bladder, stomach, large intestine,
and small intestine; excrement, urine, nasal mucus, saliva, spittle, foam, sweat, phlegm, fat, grease, membranes, sinews, and tendons—
all such impure things within the body are completely eliminated and severed.
His body was like lapis lazuli, transparent both within and without;
among the goddesses of eloquence, the various devas, and the arhats,
he was the foremost leader of all the six supernormal powers and the divine immortals.
Regarding this medicine, one must strictly avoid the five pungent roots, as well as alcohol, meat, sexual desire, and the like.
Furthermore, if one wishes to enter the dragon palace in the ocean to retrieve the wish-fulfilling jewel from the left ear of a dragon:
First, recite the aforementioned mantra ten thousand times.
Take three *liang* of sweet flag root and pound it together with benzoin.
Facing the image of Śākyamuni,
one makes pills of white honey,
each about the size of a bean.
Recite the mantra one hundred and eight times.
Bind it extensively upon the aforementioned altar and burn the medicinal substances within the altar.
It shall cause those dragon palaces to tremble violently and collapse, the great ocean to dry up,
and the palaces of all those dragon kings and asura kings to be shattered into fine dust.
The dragon will be terrified and not know what to do.
If one wishes to cause the traveler to recover and learn what is required,
one should take white honey and sweet *sugandhaka* (spikenard) and mix them with that medicine, then burn it as an incense offering.
A certain dragon, having become awakened and knowing that this person requires this precious jewel,
shall offer it with both hands to the practitioner,
desiring to restore the dragon palace and the asura palace to their former state.
"Do not burn those medicines;
the palace shall then return to its former state.
Furthermore, World-Honored One:
If one wishes to practice this method for Mañjuśrī’s salvation from myriad illnesses,
one should take five *liang* of *harītakī* fruit, pound and sift them together.
First, recite the aforementioned mantra one hundred and eight times.
He immediately knelt before the Buddha with palms joined,
single-mindedly generating a heart of great compassion and regarding him as a King of Physicians.
Take the milk of a man and mix it thoroughly.
Afterwards, recite [the mantra] one thousand and eight times.
Offer it to the Buddha for three days, and thereafter take it to treat the illness.
World-Honored One, if a person suffers from muteness,
by taking a small portion of this [medicine], they will be able to speak within one hundred days.
Furthermore, if a person suffers from eye disease, [the same applies].
In a deep chamber, protect against the wind;
by applying medicinal ointment for three days, one will recover.
Furthermore, there is another method: if one suffers from deafness.
Take the medicine and mix it with white glue; apply it as drops and the ailment will be cured immediately.
Furthermore, another method: if a person suffers from pain, applying the medicine will cause it to be cured.
Furthermore, according to another method, if a person suffers from lameness,
they will recover in seven days by applying this medicinal ointment.
Moreover, according to another method, if a person suffers from any of the thirty-six types of major wind-disorders (vāta), [they shall be cured].
Take the medicine and mix it with well-water to drink;
one will recover in three days.

Furthermore, there is another method: if one wishes to restrain the hundreds of snakes and insects, as well as various large beasts—such as elephants, horses, oxen, sheep, birds, and sparrows—within the mountains so that they all become unsettled, [one should proceed as follows].
One should take three chi of cypress wood, four inches wide,
and write the prohibitory text upon it, mixing the medicinal herbs [with the ink]. The text is as follows:
No insects or beasts shall be allowed on the mountain;
if you use them, I shall harm both you and me.
He diligently inscribed this text upon a wooden board before the Buddha,
then recited the aforementioned mantra three thousand times and drove stakes into a high mountain.
Within seven days, wild beasts will arrive at that place where the text is located;
furthermore, hundreds of insects, birds, sparrows, vipers, snakes,
dung beetles, and crickets— all manner of creatures— will gather together at that spot.
Furthermore, according to another method, if one wishes to cause a wooden post to transform,
one should take a small portion of the medicine, mix it with water, and sprinkle it [upon the wood].
Within three days, it will become a great *pīpal* tree.
Furthermore, there is another method: if one wishes to cause a person to attain longevity, one should take the medicine and mix it with well-water from morning dew, reciting the mantra seven times.
Upon consuming it, one's life span will be extended by three kalpas.
Furthermore, according to another method, if one wishes to cause an old person to become young again,
one should take raw honey, mix it with the medicine, and apply it to the face and hair; immediately,
one will resemble a man or woman of thirty-five years of age.
Furthermore, according to another method, if one wishes to cause others to feel affection and joy,
one should take the medicine, combine it with gold, and wear it as a belt; thus,
all people will respect and love them.
Furthermore, according to another method, if one wishes to expound the sublime Dharma,
one should take the medicine and apply it to the heart;
then, before the assembly, the tongue will be empowered and the mind opened for eloquence.
Furthermore, according to another method, if one wishes to cause a person to become handsome,
they should take the medicine, mix it with water, and wash their face;
within several days, they will become handsome.
Furthermore, according to another method, if one wishes to cause the cessation of the five grains,
one should take the medicine mixed with dates and consume it;
within twenty-one days, the condition will be cured and one will cease eating them.
Furthermore, according to another method, if a person is plagued by many maggots or suffers from malignant envy and taboos,
one should take the medicine and apply it to the heart;
immediately, there will be no more maggots, nor will malignant envy and taboos persist.
Furthermore, according to another method, if a person is excessively greedy,
one should take the medicine and mix it with copper powder and administer it to them;
they will then no longer be greedy.
Furthermore, according to another method, if a person is excessively lustful, one should take this medicine and give it to them to consume; after seven days, they will never again experience lust.
Furthermore, according to another method, if a person has committed many acts of killing:
